dependency_coverage.name: NumStability.HDP.Scalar.Preliminaries.absoluteMoment
dependency_coverage.interpretation: Defines the absolute moment at a real exponent as the ENNReal-valued lower integral of ENNReal.ofReal applied to |X| raised by Real.rpow.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Makes the target's absolute-moment conjunct a definitional identity for every measure, function, and positive real p.
dependency_coverage.source_match: The integrand matches |X|^p, but the ENNReal codomain, lower-integral semantics, and total applicability are conventions not supplied by the source sentence or footnotes.

dependency_coverage.name: NumStability.HDP.Scalar.Preliminaries.expectation
dependency_coverage.interpretation: Defines expectation as Mathlib's real-valued Bochner integral.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies the expectation used by rawMoment and by the right side of the raw-moment equality.
dependency_coverage.source_match: It agrees with the source's Lebesgue-expectation reading in the ordinary integrable probability setting, but the target uses it for arbitrary measures and arbitrary functions without the source's random-variable context or an integrability condition.

dependency_coverage.name: NumStability.HDP.Scalar.Preliminaries.rawMoment
dependency_coverage.interpretation: Defines rawMoment only at a natural exponent n as the expectation of X^n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Makes the first conjunct a definitional identity over n : Nat, including n = 0.
dependency_coverage.source_match: The source prints a raw moment E[X^p] for unrestricted positive real p. Replacing that exponent by a natural n repairs the negative-base obstruction but changes the stated domain and includes zero.

dependency_coverage.name: And
dependency_coverage.interpretation: Forms the conjunction of the raw-moment and absolute-moment equalities.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Requires both displayed identities simultaneously.
dependency_coverage.source_match: The source sentence presents both definitions together, so conjunction itself is appropriate; the parameter mismatch arises from the binders, not from And.

dependency_coverage.name: ENNReal
dependency_coverage.interpretation: The extended nonnegative real type WithTop NNReal.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Makes absoluteMoment capable of taking the value +∞.
dependency_coverage.source_match: The source does not state an extended-value convention for E[|X|^p], so selecting ENNReal is an unsupported semantic choice.

dependency_coverage.name: ENNReal.ofReal
dependency_coverage.interpretation: Maps a real to its nonnegative part viewed in ENNReal.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Embeds the real rpow value into the ENNReal integrand.
dependency_coverage.source_match: For |X| and p > 0 the rpow value is nonnegative, so the truncation does not alter the intended |X|^p integrand.

dependency_coverage.name: Eq
dependency_coverage.interpretation: Propositional equality.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Expresses each moment definition as an exact equality.
dependency_coverage.source_match: This matches the source phrase 'is defined as'.

dependency_coverage.name: HPow.hPow
dependency_coverage.interpretation: Dispatches exponentiation through the selected heterogeneous-power instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: On the raw side it resolves to real base and natural exponent, not real base and real exponent.
dependency_coverage.source_match: Its instantiated exponent type implements the corrected natural-exponent interface rather than the source's unrestricted positive-real raw exponent.

dependency_coverage.name: LT.lt
dependency_coverage.interpretation: The strict-order relation supplied by the relevant LT instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Expresses the hypothesis 0 < p for the real absolute-moment exponent.
dependency_coverage.source_match: This agrees with the source's strict positivity condition.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasurableSpace
dependency_coverage.interpretation: Provides a sigma-algebra on the sample type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies the measurable-space structure required by the measure and integrals.
dependency_coverage.source_match: This corresponds to the source's sigma-algebra Σ, although the target does not require X itself to be measurable.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.Measure
dependency_coverage.interpretation: An arbitrary measure on the supplied measurable space.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Quantifies the identities over every measure μ.
dependency_coverage.source_match: Footnote 1 places X on a probability space, while the target neither assumes nor records that μ is a probability measure.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral
dependency_coverage.interpretation: The ENNReal-valued lower Lebesgue integral of a nonnegative extended-real integrand.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Defines the absolute-moment value even when it is infinite and without an explicit integrability hypothesis.
dependency_coverage.source_match: It realizes a plausible extended nonnegative integral, but the source only identifies expectation with a Lebesgue integral and does not authorize this particular total extended-value convention.

dependency_coverage.name: Monoid.toNatPow
dependency_coverage.interpretation: Builds natural-number exponentiation from the real multiplicative monoid.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Makes X^n an ordinary natural power defined for negative real X.
dependency_coverage.source_match: This is the mathematical correction that avoids nonintegral powers of negative values, but it is not the unrestricted positive-real exponent printed by the source.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat
dependency_coverage.interpretation: The natural-number type, including zero.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Serves as the raw-moment exponent domain.
dependency_coverage.source_match: The source's raw exponent is positive real; Nat both omits positive nonintegers and adds n = 0.

dependency_coverage.name: OfNat.ofNat
dependency_coverage.interpretation: Interprets the numeral zero in the ambient type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Constructs the real zero used in 0 < p.
dependency_coverage.source_match: This faithfully represents the zero in the source positivity condition.

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.interpretation: The real-number type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Makes X real-valued and makes the absolute exponent p real.
dependency_coverage.source_match: Footnote 1 explicitly has X : Ω → R, and the audited reading takes p to range over positive reals.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAddGroup
dependency_coverage.interpretation: The additive-group structure on the reals.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supports real negation and hence the absolute-value operation.
dependency_coverage.source_match: This is standard infrastructure for the source's real-valued |X|.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLT
dependency_coverage.interpretation: The usual strict order on the reals.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Gives 0 < p its ordinary real-order meaning.
dependency_coverage.source_match: This matches the printed positivity condition.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMonoid
dependency_coverage.interpretation: The multiplicative monoid structure on the reals.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Provides ordinary repeated multiplication for natural powers X^n.
dependency_coverage.source_match: The operation is correct for integer raw moments but implements the target's unstated natural-exponent restriction.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instZero
dependency_coverage.interpretation: The usual zero of the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies the lower endpoint in the positivity hypothesis.
dependency_coverage.source_match: This agrees with the source.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.lattice
dependency_coverage.interpretation: The lattice order on the reals.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supports the max-based real absolute-value definition.
dependency_coverage.source_match: This is consistent with the source's ordinary real absolute value.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.rpow
dependency_coverage.interpretation: Real exponentiation implemented as the real part of complex exponentiation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Computes |X|^p for the real exponent p in the absolute-moment integrand.
dependency_coverage.source_match: Because the base is |X| ≥ 0 and p > 0, it represents the ordinary positive-real power required by the absolute-moment clause.

dependency_coverage.name: Zero.toOfNat0
dependency_coverage.interpretation: Turns a Zero instance into the interpretation of numeral 0.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Connects real zero to the positivity expression.
dependency_coverage.source_match: This is harmless elaboration of the source's 0.

dependency_coverage.name: abs
dependency_coverage.interpretation: Defines absolute value as max(a, -a) in a lattice-ordered additive group.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Transforms X into the nonnegative base |X| before real exponentiation.
dependency_coverage.source_match: This matches the source's absolute-moment integrand |X|^p.

dependency_coverage.name: instHPow

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: PDF page 1, printed page 5 states that for p > 0 the p-th moment is E[X^p] and the p-th absolute moment is E[|X|^p]; footnotes 1–2 specify the probability-space, real-valued, Lebesgue-integral, and binding conventions.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The hash-verified packet targets the separately named corrected moments interface and exposes both elaborated equalities.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The selected source passage and its permitted inherited footnotes are identified exactly.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: The printed definition uses a positive-real p for both moments, with real-valued X on a probability space.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The raw exponent is n : Nat, the absolute exponent is p : Real, μ is an arbitrary Measure, and X is merely Ω → Real.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The raw exponent type, exponent sharing, measure type, and random-variable requirements do not match.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: One p > 0 scopes over both the raw and absolute p-th moments in the source sentence.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The target independently quantifies n : Nat and p : Real and assumes positivity only for p.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The two source clauses concern the same exponent, whereas the target permits unrelated exponents.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: Footnote 1 supplies a probability space and a real-valued random variable, and the sentence requires p > 0.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The target assumes 0 < p but imposes no positivity on n, no probability-measure condition, no measurability of X, and no integrability condition.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: Only the absolute exponent's positivity is preserved; the remaining applicability conditions differ or are omitted.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: The source defines both E[X^p] and E[|X|^p] for every printed positive-real p.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The target gives raw moments only as E[X^n] for n : Nat and gives the absolute moment for a separate real p.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: Positive nonintegral raw-moment cases are absent, so the printed raw conclusion is not completely represented.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: Footnote 2 makes E[X^p] and E[|X|^p] expectations of the powered integrands, and footnote 1 calls expectation a Lebesgue integral.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The raw side uses NatPow and a real Bochner integral; the absolute side uses Real.rpow followed by ENNReal.ofReal and lintegral.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The absolute integrand is represented correctly, but the raw power is restricted and the two integrals adopt totalization and codomain conventions absent from the source.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: Each source notion 'is defined as' the stated expectation.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The target uses equality for each clause and conjoins the two equalities.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: At fixed admissible parameters, the connective and equality strength match; the substantive failures are in domains and semantics.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: The same source object p indexes both the p-th raw moment and the p-th absolute moment.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The target replaces that one role by independent objects n and p.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The identity and shared role of the exponent are not preserved.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: The index range is p > 0 in both source expressions.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The raw index range is all Nat, including zero, while only the independent absolute exponent is restricted by 0 < p.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The raw exponent range both omits positive nonintegers and adds zero.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: The source concerns a real-valued random variable on a probability space and an unrestricted positive-real raw exponent.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The target specializes raw exponents to Nat while generalizing from probability measures and random variables to arbitrary measures and functions.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: These are consequential specialization and generalization changes, not a definitionally harmless reformulation.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: For the printed allowed case p = 1/2 and a real-valued X taking value -1, X^p has no ordinary real value; no signed, complex, absolute, or integer-only convention is supplied.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The raw interface avoids that case by using Nat exponents, includes n = 0, and totalizes its integral; the absolute interface separately uses nonnegative-base Real.rpow and ENNReal lintegral.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The corrected target resolves rather than represents the source's negative-input obstruction and also makes additional boundary choices.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: Ordinary probability spaces, real random variables, and positive exponents provide nonempty intended cases.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The target hypotheses are satisfiable, for example with a probability measure, a measurable constant function, n = 1, and p = 1.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The target is nonvacuous; its definitional equalities are intentional for an interface theorem, although that interface differs from the source.

lean_implies_source.reasoning: The Lean proposition has no raw-moment assertion for a general positive real exponent. In particular it cannot yield the printed raw clause at p = 1/2; for negative-valued X that printed case also exposes the documented absence of any real-power convention. The natural-exponent correction therefore does not imply the unrestricted printed definition.

source_implies_lean.reasoning: The source speaks about one positive-real p on a probability space and a real-valued random variable. It does not imply the target's independently quantified n : Nat and p : Real, its n = 0 case, its assertions for arbitrary measures and arbitrary functions, or its particular Bochner-integral and ENNReal-lintegral totalizations.

findings.source_evidence: The source defines E[X^p] for unrestricted positive-real p and permits real-valued X; p = 1/2 with negative X exposes an unresolved real-power obstruction.
findings.lean_evidence: The corrected interface instead defines rawMoment only for n : Nat using ordinary natural powers.
findings.impact: This is a substantive repair and restriction, not a faithful rendering of the printed definition; the target omits the source's nonintegral raw cases.

findings.source_evidence: A single p > 0 indexes both source notions.
findings.lean_evidence: Independent n and p index the two Lean notions, and n may equal zero.
findings.impact: The target can pair unrelated moment orders and asserts a raw zero-th moment outside the printed positive range.

findings.source_evidence: Footnote 1 places the real-valued random variable on a probability space.
findings.lean_evidence: The target quantifies over an arbitrary measure and arbitrary real-valued function without probability, measurability, or integrability assumptions.
findings.impact: The target has materially different applicability, so the source cannot imply the full Lean proposition.

findings.source_evidence: The page calls expectation a Lebesgue integral but states no finiteness, nonintegrability, or extended-value convention for these moments.
findings.lean_evidence: Raw expectation is a totalized real Bochner integral, while absoluteMoment is an ENNReal-valued lintegral.
findings.impact: The formalization chooses behavior and result types for exceptional cases that the permitted source passage leaves unspecified.

rationale: The target is a coherent, separately named corrected interface: natural exponents make raw powers real-valued even for negative X, and positive real exponents remain available for absolute moments. That correction is mathematically useful but does not faithfully reproduce the printed unrestricted positive-real definition. It also splits the source's one exponent into two independent parameters, includes raw order zero, generalizes beyond probability spaces and random variables, and selects unstated integral totalizations. These established differences make both implication directions fail, so the classification is not-faithful-different without a need for adjudication.
